context: Sortable data table with embedded sparklines showing 12-month line-count growth across 25 D3 skill categories
first_impression: A polished, professional-feeling table with a deliberate Tableau-derived category palette and clean typographic hierarchy, but the sparklines — the headline visual element — are nearly flat horizontal lines that fail to communicate growth.
what_works: The category color palette is genuinely intentional (not schemeCategory10) and applied consistently across dots, sparkline strokes, and area fills, creating coherent visual grouping; typography hierarchy is well-executed with uppercased letter-spaced headers, bold skill names, muted category labels, and monospace tabular numerals for the Change % column.
what_doesnt: Sparklines use a global y-domain mapped against the full data range (~50–900 lines), which compresses individual growth curves into near-horizontal dashes — the core encoding fails to show what the chart promises; the area fills at 0.1 opacity add almost no visual information and could be removed without loss.
